Currently responsible for managing the temple's affairs, Ms. Ying (a pseudonym) from the Chow family descendants revealed to a photojournalist that years ago, her grandfather, a Tanka fisherman, unexpectedly retrieved a wooden sculpture of 'Fourth Sister' while out at sea. Her grandfather brought the carving home and gave it to young Ying as a toy, and she even sewed clothes for the statue. Unexpectedly, Ying then fell ill with a high fever, and her grandmother received a dream visitation from 'Seventh Sister', who instructed the grandfather to have the statue enshrined in a temple. The Chow family thus followed the divine oracle and built the present-day Seven Sisters Temple.

The Fairy Sister Temple is renowned for its efficacy in seeking romantic matches, and Ms. Ying shared a romantic anecdote. On the evening of the sixth day of the seventh lunar month three years ago, a slightly chubby man with a bit of 'baby fat' waited patiently in front of the temple until midnight of the seventh day to pay his respects, and did the same the following year. Until yesterday evening of the sixth day, that man, dressed in red, came with his girlfriend in hand to fulfil his vow. Ms. Ying initially did not notice, until he awkwardly smiled at her while holding his girlfriend's hand, and she finally recognised this devoted suitor, witnessing the blossoming of a destined match.

When discussing the insights for worshipping at the Seven Sisters Temple, Ms. Ying believes it is essentially about communicating with the deities: 'Just say it directly, tell Seventh Sister your worries.' Like having a 'chat', if one wishes to know Seventh Sister's advice and outcome, one can cast divination blocks. During the Qixi Festival, the Fairy Sister Temple is not only a sacred place for seeking blessed romantic unions, but also a haven for devotees to unburden their hearts.
